title: Merit badge popularity ranking (one year)
description: One immutable document per year: data/merit-badge-rankings/<year>.json, ranking every merit badge offered that year by how many were earned. NOT an entity — it has no versions and is never revised, like a requirement-set. ⚠ Scouting America publishes RANKS ONLY. Its annual recap gives each badge a position and no absolute earned-count anywhere, so `metric` is 'earned_rank' and consumers must not infer volume: the gap between rank 1 and rank 2 is unknown and unknowable from this source.

id.description: The data year, as a string, matching both `year` and the filename stem.

year.description: The calendar year the ranking describes — not the year it was published.

metric.description: What the numbers mean. Only 'earned_rank' exists because it is the only thing published: position by number of badges earned, 1 = most earned. A future 'earned_count' metric would be additive if Scouting America ever releases volumes.

complete.description: True when the ranks form an unbroken 1..N covering every badge offered that year, which the pipeline verifies. False would mean a partially recovered year; consumers should not compute 'least earned' from an incomplete year.

year.description: Publication year of the source post, normally the data year + 1.

rank.description: 1 = most earned. Ranks are unique within a year; the pipeline rejects duplicates and, for a complete year, gaps.

subject.description: The merit badge, e.g. 'merit-badge:first-aid'. Resolved against the badge's own lifecycle: a badge cannot be ranked in a year it did not exist, which is what catches a source printing a pre-rename name (the 2022 post still says 'Medicine' two years after it became Health Care Professions).
